frame.origin: contact point under the body centre (rock / perch top / water surface)

authoring: Generated by CormorantIso.gameplayGeometry() from the same BODY/POSE/MOTION tables the bake uses. Do not hand-edit — re-generate (docs/art/rigs/birds/tools/build.cjs --write).
extractor_contract: per section: rig export -> this sidecar -> absent section = the creature does not support the feature (not an error).

fly.note: low and straight over the water, neck out; never wheels or soars

glide.note: a short flat glide on the way in; not a soaring state

dive.note: from float only: a forward leap, bill first, and gone. Not a plunge from the air

surface.note: head and neck first; the page places it at the end of the UNDER spell

splash.note: water landing: feet first, skis, settles; splashRig.js burst at f1

float.note: swims low, bill tilted up; paddles under its own power

patter.note: the run along the water: both wings beating, feet striking; splashRig.js small burst every frame 0 and 2

stand.note: nearly upright, propped on its tail

dry.note: wings held half open to dry, slow fanning. Reached from stand and perch only

perch.note: contact plane = the perch top (piling, buoy, ledge lip)

takeoff.note: from stand / perch / dry: drops forward off the perch and beats away low

UNDER.note: "under" is a STATE WITH NO FRAMES: between dive and surface the bird is not drawn. The page hides it for spell_s, moves it travel_m (toward fish if it knows where they are), and plays surface there. A ring of ripples at the dive point and at the surfacing point is the page's (splashRig.js, smallest burst). After dives_before_drying dives it flies to a perch and plays dry.

DRY.note: The pose that makes it a cormorant: upright, wings held half open, slow fanning. Only on a perch or flat rock clear of the water. Faces into the wind when there is one (page turns the facing; the rig is the same).

LAND.note: land() ends in stand (rock, ledge, breakwater) or perch (a piling or buoy top). It does not land on sand flats, grass, roofs or decks.

PERCH.note: The pivot sits ON the surface. A cormorant wants a top it can stand its whole foot on and room for the tail behind it.

WATER.note: float pivots at the surface with the body centre BELOW it (float_body_z is negative): the back is awash and the tail is under. Pixels under the surface are baked as the depth tint, as the gull's. It cannot take off from the water in one jump: float -> patter (a loop the page holds for cycles) -> fly.

dive_yield.note: a dive is a hunt; the page rolls a catch at surface f0
dive_yield.catch_species_note: small bottom and mid-water fish; the game's species data names them

GROUP.note: Loose company, not a wheeling flock: a few on a ledge, one or two fishing, a short line flying low to the next spot. The gull's attractors (gutting, tubs, bait) do NOT draw it: it hunts its own fish.
GROUP.flee_reaction: takeoff (from a perch) or dive (from the water)

ANCHORS_PX.note: screen offsets from the pivot at dir 0 (bill toward N); use CormorantIso.anchors(dir,{anim,frame}) for the rest

FIELD_NOTES.species: Double-crested cormorant, Nannopterum auritum: the common breeding cormorant of the Maritimes' harbours and estuaries in the warm months. The great cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo) is the winter bird of the outer coast: bigger, white throat and flank patch. Not drawn; it could be a second look on this body.
FIELD_NOTES.sizes: length 70-90 cm, wingspan 114-123 cm, mass 1.2-2.5 kg (the brief's figures; the rig draws 0.82 m and 1.20 m). To be confirmed against a field guide by title, edition and page before the look is called final.
FIELD_NOTES.marks: adult in breeding dress: all black with a green gloss, bronze-brown upperwing coverts edged dark, bare orange-yellow throat skin and lores, dusky hooked bill, aquamarine eye, black legs and webs. The crests are a few thin plumes for a few weeks in spring and are not drawn at this size.

_excluded.states: No swoop, preen, peck or walk: a cormorant does not wheel over a boat, and on land it stands. No plunge from the air: its dive starts from the water.
_excluded.looks: One look: the breeding adult. The pale-breasted first-year bird and the great cormorant are not drawn — absence is data.
_excluded.skinned_export: No skeleton / bindMesh / clips. This rig ships on the sprite-sheet route the herring gull is on today.
_excluded.sound: Calls belong to the audio lane; a cormorant is near silent away from the colony.
